# pH drift in recirculating hydroponic reservoirs

A recirculating reservoir drifts upward whenever the crop absorbs more nitrate
anions than cations, because the plant excretes bicarbonate to keep charge
balance. The drift is a consequence of uptake, not a dosing mistake, so the
correction has to be small and frequent.

## Alkalinity and acid dosing

Measure alkalinity in milligrams of calcium carbonate per litre before touching
the acid bottle: a reservoir with 120 mg/L of alkalinity will pull the pH back up
within hours of any correction. Dosing nitric or phosphoric acid by hand, in
steps of two tenths of a pH unit, keeps the root zone stable and avoids the
calcium precipitation that a single large correction produces.

Calibrate the probe against fresh buffer every fortnight; a probe reading two
tenths low sends the whole schedule chasing a drift that does not exist.
